newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-SCHOLL KEEN TO HIT GOALS -- NOT FACES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-SCHOLL KEEN TO HIT GOALS -- NOT FACES.

text.p: Mehmet Scholl's temper and tongue can be as sharp as his shooting. This time the Bayern Munich player wants to be remembered for hitting goals -- not faces -- in Germany's match-of-the-season on Sunday.
In last season's corresponding Bundesliga clash between Bayern and champions Borussia Dortmund, Scholl produced a superb lob to clinch a 1-0 victory.

But the game was remembered for the swipe he took at Dortmund striker Stephane Chapuisat at the end of a bruising encounter when the Swiss forward provoked the midfielder by striking him in the back of the legs.
German Euro 96 player Scholl, who tends to speak his mind in public, is not Borussia's favourite opponent after making some critical comments about Dortmund in the past.
Whatever happens in Munich's Olympic stadium on Sunday evening, the talented player, known for his dribbling skills and deadly shooting, is certain to be at the centre of attention.
But this time he wants to avoid negative headlines.

Asked how he would greet Chapuisat at the weekend, Scholl said: "I will try to play like I played last year and stay away from things like that. But I won't exactly be looking to make contact with him.
"The team that wins the championship must win their home games. We want to keep up our good form at home."
Chapuisat is a classic goal poacher. Despite his small frame, he is not afraid of looking after himself against tough defenders and has a reputation for being an awkward customer.
Dortmund will be missing their main characters in fiery libero Matthias Sammer and playmaker Andy Moeller who are both injured. The pressure will be on Chapuisat to play a leading role for Dortmund.
Asked about last season's incident, the Swiss said: "That is all old hat. I made the mistake of getting involved in it all."
But the striker knows that there will be tension in the top-of-the-table clash again.
"This game is just one of 34 in the season. But in the present circumstances it is very important that we don't lose it," he said.
